subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw make Gemini-style quota buckets a first-class native provider/auth routing concept, or keep this as evidence under the broader provider-profile pool-routing design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41135?
rationale: The remaining work would add public config/state semantics for provider keys, auth profiles, cooldown scope, and status output; automation should not choose those product boundaries or defaults.

options.title: Fold Into Provider Pool Design
options.body: Keep this issue open as bucket-specific evidence while the broader provider-profile routing contract defines bucket identity and cooldown semantics.

options.title: Narrow Native Key-Bucket Feature
options.body: Approve a smaller API-key-pool design for Gemini project buckets before the full provider-profile routing work lands.

options.title: Sidecar Or Plugin Only
options.body: Decline native bucket routing for now and document external sidecars or future plugin hooks as the supported path.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provider Pool Design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as bucket-specific evidence while the broader provider-profile routing contract defines bucket identity and cooldown semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocker is product/config direction across auth and provider routing, and steipete has the strongest current history in those boundaries.
